prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofing company that fits every homeowner — the right choice depends on your exact location, roof type, budget, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and the level of warranty/service you want. I can help you find the best option for your situation. A good next step is to tell me your ZIP code, whether this is residential or commercial, and if you have an asphalt-shingle, tile, metal, or other roof.

Meanwhile, here’s a short, practical guide so you can identify the best local contractor:

What to require and verify
- License and insurance: Verify the contractor has a Texas roofing license (if required for your project), general liability insurance, and workers’ comp. Ask for certificates you can call to confirm.  
- Local presence and track record: Prefer companies with a stable local office and recent local references.  
- Manufacturer certifications: Look for GAF/IKO/Atlas/CertainTeed certification — this enables extended warranties.  
- Written estimate and scope: Get 3 detailed, written estimates that list materials, brand/model, underlayment, ventilation, flashing, number of tear-off layers, disposal, start/finish dates, and payment schedule.  
- Warranties: Distinguish between manufacturer (shingle) warranty and contractor workmanship warranty. Get both in writing.  
- Permits and cleanup: Contractor should pull required permits and handle inspections and disposal.  
- References and reviews: Check Google Reviews, Yelp, BBB, and ask for 3 recent local references (completed within last 6–12 months).  
- Payment terms: Avoid large up-front payments (>30%). Do not pay in full until work passes inspection and you have lien waivers.

Questions to ask every bidder
- “Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I want?”  
- “Will you remove old roof (tear-off) or overlay?”  
- “What underlayment, ice & water shield, and ventilation will you install?”  
- “Who will supervise the crew and how do you handle punch-list items?”  
- “Can you provide proof of insurance and a list of recent Dallas-area jobs I can contact?”

Red flags
- High-pressure sales, “storm-chaser” tactics, or a company that won’t provide a written estimate.  
- Vague answers about permits, insurance, or warranties.  
- Requests for full payment up-front or cash-only deals.  
- No physical address or only cell-phone contact.

Estimated cost (Dallas, ballpark)
- Asphalt shingle roof for a typical 1,800–2,200 sq ft home: roughly $5,000–$15,000 depending on roof complexity and shingle grade. Metal, tile, or architectural shingles are more. Get written bids — prices vary widely.

If you’d like, I can:
- Find highly rated Dallas roofers near your ZIP code and return a short vetted list (3–5) with key notes; or  
- Draft an email/phone script you can use when contacting contractors; or  
- Walk you through reviewing 3 specific estimates you already have.

Tell me your ZIP code and a couple of details (residential vs commercial, roof material, insurance claim?) and I’ll pull a tailored short list.
